name: @projexlight/sdk-onprem
summary: On-premises deployment variant for ProjexCloud: install registry, signed bundle application, optional local-LLM model registry, air-gapped billing report uploads. Lets a regulated tenant run the entire ProjexCloud stack inside their own data center with periodic billing/health uploads to the SaaS control plane. P8 deployment-variant artifact.

events.name: onprem.install.registered.v1
events.description: New on-prem install registered with the SaaS control plane.

events.name: onprem.bundle.applied.v1
events.description: A signed bundle was applied to an on-prem install.

events.name: onprem.local_llm.registered.v1
events.description: Local LLM model registered (vLLM / llama.cpp endpoint).

events.name: onprem.billing.uploaded.v1
events.description: Periodic billing snapshot uploaded back to the SaaS billing pipeline.

events.name: onprem.heartbeat.received.v1
events.description: Health heartbeat from the on-prem install.

models.description: Per-install row: customer, region, deployed_version, public_key (for signed bundles).
Per-bundle-apply row: install_id, bundle_id, signature_verified, applied_at.
Per-(install, model) row: provider (vllm/llama.cpp/ollama), endpoint, allowed_uses.
Per-report row: install_id, period, usage_event_count, snapshot_hash.

hooks.name: registerInstall
hooks.description: Register a new on-prem install with the SaaS control plane (manual customer-led ceremony).

hooks.name: applyBundle
hooks.description: Apply a signed bundle to an install; refuses unverified signatures.

hooks.name: registerLocalLlm
hooks.description: Register a local LLM endpoint so sdk-ai-gateway routes through it.

hooks.name: uploadBillingReport
hooks.description: Periodic upload — on-prem install sends a usage snapshot to the SaaS billing pipeline (out-of-band; usually weekly).

hooks.name: startHeartbeat
hooks.description: Background worker — sends health heartbeats to the SaaS control plane.

scenarios.title: Customer registers their on-prem install with SaaS control plane
scenarios.when_to_use: Initial on-prem deployment. Customer generates a keypair locally; registers the public key with the SaaS control plane; that's how subsequent bundles get signed against them.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Install row + emits .install.registered.v1. Customer can now receive signed bundles.

scenarios.title: Customer applies a signed product bundle
scenarios.when_to_use: SaaS publishes a new bundle (signed against this install's public key); customer downloads + applies. Signature verification mandatory.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Signature verified + bundle applied. Emits .bundle.applied.v1 with the version. Failed-signature aborts the apply atomically.

scenarios.title: Register the tenant's local vLLM endpoint
scenarios.when_to_use: Air-gapped tenant runs their own local LLM; register so sdk-ai-gateway routes prompt traffic to it instead of external providers.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Model row written. sdk-ai-gateway picks it up via its provider registry refresh.

scenarios.title: Weekly billing snapshot upload
scenarios.when_to_use: Background worker — once a week the install uploads aggregated usage to the SaaS billing pipeline so finance can invoice.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Snapshot signed locally + posted to SaaS billing endpoint. Hash stored on both sides for integrity. Emits .billing.uploaded.v1.

scenarios.title: Heartbeat sweeper alerts when an install goes dark
scenarios.when_to_use: Background worker sends heartbeats; SaaS side notices a 30-min gap + alerts the customer-success oncall.
scenarios.example_code:
import { startHeartbeat } from '@projexlight/sdk-onprem';
startHeartbeat({ install_id, interval_min: 5 });
scenarios.expected_outcome: Heartbeat .received.v1 lands every 5 min on the SaaS side. Missing heartbeats alert via sdk-notification.

compliance_posture.notes: Customer keeps all PII inside their own data center; only aggregated usage uploads to SaaS — the GDPR Art-44 + ITAR + FedRAMP air-gap posture. Bundle signature verification mandatory; tampered bundles refused. Local LLM registration is the air-gapped tenant's escape valve from external AI providers.
